note.amb.x: There are several definitions with this name. Unqualified references are then ambiguous – better write Package::Name in the model.
note.c-attributes.x: Properties with a type and possibly a value, e.g. mass or capacity.
note.c-directed features.x: Features with a direction: in = comes in, out = goes out. Typical in port defs and actions.
note.c-ends.x: The two ends of a connection type – which port types it connects.
note.c-literals.x: The fixed values of an enumeration.
note.c-parts.x: The parts this element consists of.
note.collapsed.x: This part contains further parts that are hidden at the chosen depth. Increase the depth above or click the part.
note.decide.x: Diamond: the process branches on conditions [ … ] or joins again.
note.def.x: A blueprint, e.g. part def. A definition describes how something is built – it only becomes part of the system once it is used.
note.e-bind.x: Both sides always have the same value.
note.e-comp.x: The whole (the side with the filled diamond) consists of the part at the arrowhead. The label gives the part's name and, if needed, its multiplicity.
note.e-conn.x: Two ports or parts are connected. A line without an arrow says nothing about a flow direction.
note.e-contain.x: The requirement with the circled plus groups the other one as a sub-requirement.
note.e-defby.x: Links a concrete usage (rounded) to its blueprint (square, at the triangle).
note.e-flow.x: Something flows in the direction of the arrow from an output to an input: data, energy or material. The label says what flows.
note.e-iface.x: Thick line: a connection whose kind is defined by an interface def. The label names that type.
note.e-inner.x: Leads to the internal structure: which parts are inside and how they are connected.
note.e-satisfy.x: The component satisfies the requirement at the arrowhead. This relationship is the core of traceability.
note.e-spec.x: The hollow triangle points to the more general definition. The other one inherits all its features and can add its own.
note.e-succ.x: The step at the arrowhead starts when the previous one has finished. [ … ] is the condition of a branch.
note.e-trans.x: Change from one state to the next. Label: trigger [guard] / effect.
note.e-typed.x: Dashed: the element is of the type of the definition at the arrowhead, or refers to it (e.g. exhibit, perform, subject).
note.feature.x: Notation: name : Type [multiplicity] = value. The type refers to a definition.
note.file.x: Frame around all definitions from one .sysml file.
note.fork.x: Bar: several steps run in parallel or wait for each other.
note.frame.x: Everything inside the frame belongs to this element. Ports on the border are its connections to the outside.
note.inherited.x: The feature is not defined here but in a more general definition – it is inherited.
note.init.x: The process or state machine begins here.
note.port-generic.x: The square on the border is a port. The triangle inside shows the direction: into the part (in) or out of it (out). Without a triangle the direction is open.
note.r-allocate.x: allocate: something logical (e.g. a process) is assigned to something physical (e.g. a computer).
note.r-connect.x: Two parts are connected via ports; the brackets name the interface and the ports.
note.r-derive.x: derivation: one requirement follows from another.
note.r-flow.x: flow: something flows from an output to an input.
note.r-owns.x: Composition: the element belongs to a larger whole or contains smaller parts.
note.r-perform.x: perform or exhibit: the component performs a process or exhibits state behaviour.
note.r-refine.x: refinement: one element describes another in more detail.
note.r-satisfy.x: satisfy: a component implements a requirement.
note.r-spec.x: Specialization :> – inherits all features of the more general definition.
note.r-subject.x: subject: what a requirement or a test refers to.
note.r-typed.x: Typing: the link between blueprint (definition) and concrete usage.
note.r-verify.x: verify: a test proves that a requirement is met.
note.redef.x: An inherited feature is redefined here, e.g. with its own value.
note.usage.x: A concrete use of a definition in a particular context, e.g. the battery inside the robot.
reqs.empty: No requirement elements in this scope.
rule.ambig.title: Name defined more than once
rule.ambig.why: Definitions with the same name in different packages are allowed, but they make unqualified references ambiguous. Package::Name makes it unique.
rule.broken.title: Dangling reference
rule.broken.why: A relationship points to a name that does not exist in the model. The relationship then has no effect – usually a typo or a missing import.
rule.direction.title: Port directions do not match
rule.direction.why: Connected ports should match: what one sends (out), the other must receive (in). Two outputs against each other are a short circuit in the model. The fix is often a conjugated port (~).
rule.emptytest.title: Test without a requirement
rule.emptytest.why: A test that verifies no requirement checks something nobody asked for – or the verify is missing.
rule.noreq.title: Component without a requirement
rule.noreq.why: Neither the component nor an assembly it belongs to satisfies a requirement. Every component should trace back to a requirement – otherwise one has to ask why it exists.
rule.openport.title: Open port
rule.openport.why: The component is used in an assembly, but this port is not connected anywhere. Either a connection is missing or the port is unnecessary.
rule.parse.title: Source text the parser did not understand
rule.parse.why: The parser skipped something here. Often it is a typo or a missing brace – then parts of the model are missing from all views.
rule.type.title: Unknown type
rule.type.why: The type after the colon is not defined anywhere. Without a definition the model does not know what this element is.
rule.unsat.title: Requirement without implementation
rule.unsat.why: No component satisfies this requirement. It is a promise without an implementation.
rule.unused.title: Definition without usage
rule.unused.why: This definition is not used anywhere: no usage, no specialization. Perhaps a leftover or a building block not yet put in place.
rule.unver.title: Requirement without a test
rule.unver.why: No test verifies this requirement. Whether the system meets it remains unproven.
sev.error.hint: The model is wrong or not fully understood at this point.
sev.gap.hint: Something is missing in the chain requirement → implementation → verification.
sev.hint.hint: Not an error, but a place worth a second look.

tour.action.x: Structure says what the system consists of, behaviour what it does. {behav} is a sequence of actions; arrows show the order, diamonds decisions.
tour.check.x: The check looks for errors (dangling references, wrong port directions), gaps and oddities – with an explanation and a code suggestion to copy.

tour.done: Tour finished – you can restart it any time from “Start”
tour.end.x: On the start page every question leads to the matching view. When you hover over lines, boxes and terms, the viewer explains the notation.
tour.iface.x: The “Connections” diagram shows {impl} together with the other parts. The small squares on the border are ports – here, for example, {port}. The triangle inside shows whether something goes in or out.
tour.impact.x: If {impl} changes, the impact view shows step by step which parts, requirements and tests are affected – each with a reason.
tour.impl.x: {impl} satisfies {req}. In the model this is a satisfy relationship. Without it no tool would know what a component is for – and no change could be traced back.
tour.req.x: Everything starts with a requirement: “{text}” It is now in focus at the top; below, the profile describes it in plain language – with everything attached to it.
tour.state.x: Structure says what the system consists of, behaviour what it does. {behav} is a state machine: boxes are states, arrows are transitions with their trigger.
tour.test.x: {test} checks {req}. The verify in the objective links the test to the requirement. Only then is the chain closed: required, implemented, verified.
tour.welcome.x: A model answers a chain of questions: {stages}. The tour follows this chain along an example from your model. Continue with the button or the → arrow key.
